table.name: car_makers
table.purpose: One row per automobile manufacturer; links maker names to their headquarter country and to the models they produce (model_list).

col_001.name: maker_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the car maker, referenced by model_list (each model belongs to one maker).

col_002.name: maker_short_name
col_002.description: Lowercase short/abbreviated maker name (e.g. 'amc', 'gm', 'bmw'); joins one-to-one to model_list.col_003, so model_list stores the maker by this short name.

col_003.name: full_name
col_003.description: Full official manufacturer name (e.g. 'General Motors', 'American Motor Company').

col_004.name: country_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to countries.col_001, the country of the maker's headquarters (e.g. 2=germany, 4=japan, 7=uk). Stored as text despite being numeric.

table.name: car_names
table.purpose: Maps each car (one row per car model variant) to its make and full model name; the ID is referenced by the cars_data table with technical specs.

col_001.name: car_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each car entry, referenced by cars_data.col_005 which holds the car's technical data.

col_002.name: make
col_002.description: Car manufacturer/make (e.g. ford, chevrolet, amc); references model_list.col_003.

col_003.name: model
col_003.description: Full model name including make (e.g. 'amc matador', 'toyota corolla'); not unique because a model can appear in multiple years/variants.

table.name: cars_data
table.purpose: Technical specifications of car models (one row per car), covering fuel economy, engine, weight, performance and model year. This is the classic 'cars' / auto-mpg style dataset.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Surrogate primary key; sequential integer 1-406, one per car row.

col_002.name: mpg
col_002.description: Fuel economy in miles per gallon (values 9.0-46.6, stored as VARCHAR).

col_005.name: horsepower
col_005.description: Engine horsepower (46-230, stored as VARCHAR). Joins to car_names.col_001, so it doubles as a link to the car's name/model record.

col_007.name: acceleration
col_007.description: Acceleration, likely 0-60 mph time in seconds (8.0-24.8; lower = faster).

table.name: continents
table.purpose: Lookup table of continents, one row per continent, referenced by the countries table.

col_001.name: continent_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate integer identifier for each continent (1-5). Referenced by countries.col_003 as a foreign key.

col_002.name: continent_name
col_002.description: Name of the continent: africa, america, asia, australia, europe. Note 'america' covers North and South America combined.

table.name: countries
table.purpose: Lookup table of countries, each mapped to its continent; referenced by car_makers to indicate a maker's home country.

col_001.name: country_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each country. Referenced by car_makers.col_004 (the maker's country).

col_002.name: country_name
col_002.description: Unique lowercase name of the country (e.g. germany, japan, uk).

col_003.name: continent_id
col_003.description: Foreign key to continents.col_001; values 1-5 map to america, europe, asia, africa, australia respectively.

table.name: model_list
table.purpose: List of car models/makes, each row a distinct car make/model entry, linked to its manufacturer (car_makers) and referenced by car_names for individual named cars.

col_001.name: model_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each model/make entry (1-36).

col_002.name: maker_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to car_makers.col_001, identifying the manufacturer of the model (e.g. 4=gm, 13=daimler benz, 16=renault).

col_003.name: model_name
col_003.description: Unique make/model name (e.g. 'buick', 'mercedes-benz', 'opel'); referenced by car_names and matched one-to-one with car_makers' maker names.
